name: City Palace
description: A sprawling complex of courtyards, mirrored halls and balconies looking over Lake Pichola.
tip: Arrive at opening to have the Mor Chowk peacock courtyard to yourself.

name: Lake Pichola sunset boat
description: A gentle hour on the water past Jag Mandir as the palaces turn gold.
tip: Take the last boat before sunset from Rameshwar Ghat.

name: Monsoon Palace
description: A hilltop palace with sweeping views of the Aravalli hills and lakes below.
tip: Share a jeep up the hill; walking the road is steep.

name: Hathi Pol Bazaar
description: Miniature paintings, silver and textiles near the old elephant gate.
tip: Ask to see artists at work before you buy.

name: Amber Fort
description: Honey-coloured ramparts and the glittering Sheesh Mahal above Maota Lake.
tip: Walk up the cobbled path in the cool of the morning.

name: Hawa Mahal
description: The Palace of Winds — 953 latticed windows built for royal women to watch street life.
tip: Best photographed from the café rooftops opposite at sunrise.

name: Johari Bazaar
description: Gemstones, lac bangles and block-printed textiles under pink arcades.
tip: Bargain with a smile; start at half the first price.

name: Galta Ji Monkey Temple
description: Temples and sacred tanks tucked into a ravine east of the city.
tip: Keep snacks out of sight — the macaques are quick.

name: Tata Tea Museum
description: See orthodox tea processing and taste fresh brews at a working factory.
tip: The tasting room sells loose-leaf at estate prices.

name: Eravikulam National Park
description: Grassland home of the rare Nilgiri tahr, with views to Anamudi peak.
tip: Closed Feb–Mar for the tahr calving season.

name: Top Station
description: A viewpoint above a sea of clouds on the Kerala–Tamil Nadu border.
tip: Go before 9am, before the mist rolls in.

name: Attukal Waterfalls
description: A forest trek ending at a tiered monsoon-fed waterfall.
tip: Wear grippy shoes — the rocks are slick.

name: Khan el-Khalili
description: A medieval souk of brass lamps, spices and perfume bottles.
tip: Stop for mint tea at El Fishawy café.

name: Grand Egyptian Museum
description: Tutankhamun's treasures and a colossal Ramses II in a vast modern hall.
tip: Book a timed ticket online to skip the queue.

name: Al-Azhar Mosque
description: Over a thousand years of prayer and scholarship in Fatimid Cairo.
tip: Dress modestly; scarves are lent at the door.

name: Great Pyramid of Khufu
description: 4,500 years old and still astonishing up close.
tip: Enter at 8am when the gates open for the coolest air.

name: Great Sphinx
description: The enigmatic guardian of the plateau, carved from a single ridge.
tip: Included with the plateau ticket.

name: Desert camel ride
description: Ride to the panoramic point for the classic nine-pyramid view.
tip: Agree the price and duration before mounting.

name: Karnak Temple
description: The Great Hypostyle Hall's 134 columns tower like a stone forest.
imageCredit: Photo: Jorge Láscar, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
tip: Return for the evening sound-and-light show.

name: Valley of the Kings
description: Painted royal tombs cut deep into the Theban hills.
tip: Ticket includes three tombs; Seti I is extra and worth it.

name: Sunrise hot-air balloon
description: Drift over temples, sugarcane fields and the Nile as the sun comes up.
tip: Flights are cancelled in high wind — keep a spare morning.

name: Echo Point
description: A lakeside spot on the Munnar–Top Station road where the surrounding hills throw your voice back across the water. Mist, tea slopes and calm water make it a favourite photo stop.
tip: Go early before tour buses arrive

name: Mattupetty Dam
description: A concrete gravity dam surrounded by shola forest and tea estates, with a reservoir popular for boating. Wild elephants are sometimes spotted along the banks.
tip: Boating slots fill up on weekends

name: Kundala Lake
description: A serene reservoir behind an arch dam, ringed by eucalyptus and tea estates. Known for shikara-style boat rides and cherry blossoms in season.
tip: Mornings are calmer for boating

name: Pothamedu Viewpoint
description: A quiet hillside viewpoint a few kilometres from town with layered views over tea, coffee and cardamom plantations.
tip: Combine with a sunrise drive

name: Lakkam Waterfalls
description: A gentle cascade on the Marayoor road with a natural pool, surrounded by forest. Less crowded than town attractions.
tip: Follow forest-department instructions about bathing

name: Kolukkumalai Sunrise Point
description: Often described as one of the highest tea estates in the world. A rough jeep track leads to a sunrise viewpoint above a sea of clouds.
tip: Leave around 4 am for sunrise

name: Munnar Town Bazaar Eateries
description: Small family-run eateries around the main bazaar serve Kerala meals on banana leaf, parotta and beef fry, and quick snacks for travellers.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Estate Tea Stalls
description: Roadside tea stalls along the estate roads pour fresh local tea with banana fritters — a classic Munnar ritual.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Edakkal Caves
description: Two natural rock shelters on Ambukuthi Mala with prehistoric petroglyphs believed to be thousands of years old. A steep climb leads to the upper chamber.
tip: Wear good shoes for the climb

name: Banasura Sagar Dam
description: One of India's largest earthen dams, with islands dotting its reservoir and the Banasura hills behind.
tip: Avoid the hottest afternoon hours

name: Pookode Lake
description: A natural freshwater lake wrapped in evergreen forest near Lakkidi, with pedal boats and a lakeside walking path.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Soochipara Waterfalls
description: A three-tiered waterfall dropping through dense forest near Meppadi, reached by a forest trail.
tip: Access may close during heavy monsoon

name: Chembra Peak
description: Wayanad's highest peak, famous for a heart-shaped lake on the way to the summit. Treks are guided and permit-controlled.
tip: Start early

name: Meenmutty Falls
description: A forest waterfall near Vaduvanchal reached by a short trek, quieter than the main circuit.
tip: Moderate forest trail; may close during the monsoon.

name: Kuruva Island
description: A cluster of river islands on the Kabini, explored on bamboo rafts and forest paths. Entry is regulated to protect the ecosystem.
tip: Raft crossings and uneven paths. Daily visitor limits apply.

name: Kalpetta Malabar Eateries
description: Simple restaurants in Kalpetta known for Malabar-style biryani, meals and bamboo rice dishes.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Kovalam Beach
description: A crescent of three beaches — Lighthouse, Hawah and Samudra — with a red-and-white lighthouse, cafés and Ayurveda resorts.
tip: Swim only in flagged zones

name: Shankumugham Beach
description: A city beach next to the airport, known for the giant Jalakanyaka (mermaid) sculpture and evening crowds.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Napier Museum
description: A 19th-century Indo-Saracenic building housing bronzes, ivory carvings and historical artefacts, set in the museum and zoo gardens.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Ponmudi
description: A hill station about 60 km from the city, reached by a road with 22 hairpin bends through forest and tea estates.
tip: Road may close in heavy rain

name: Varkala Beach
description: A beach at the foot of dramatic laterite cliffs, with a clifftop walkway of cafés and the ancient Janardanaswamy temple nearby. Also called Papanasam beach.
tip: Currents can be strong — swim with lifeguards nearby

name: Poovar Estuary
description: Where the Neyyar river meets the sea — a golden sand bar between backwater and ocean, reached by boat through mangroves.
tip: Boat-only access to the sand bar; operators vary in quality.

name: Kappil Beach
description: A quiet stretch north of Varkala where the Edava–Nadayara backwater lies right beside the sea.
tip: Roadside access; few facilities.

name: Chalai & East Fort Street Food
description: The old market area around East Fort is a good place to try local snacks, tea and traditional sweets.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Chinese Fishing Nets
description: Giant cantilevered fishing nets along the Fort Kochi shoreline — an iconic sight, especially at sunset.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Mattancherry Palace
description: Also called the Dutch Palace, known for its Kerala murals depicting Hindu epics.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Jew Town & Paradesi Synagogue
description: Antique shops and spice warehouses line the lane to the 16th-century Paradesi Synagogue.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Kashi Art Café
description: A long-standing Fort Kochi café that doubles as an art gallery, known for breakfasts and cakes.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Fort Kochi Seafood Stalls
description: Stalls beside the fishing nets will cook the seafood you buy from fishermen, Kerala-style.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Kumbalangi Village
description: An island village of backwaters, Chinese nets and fishing traditions, promoted as a model tourism village.
tip: Village roads; best explored by bicycle or canoe with a local guide.

name: Punnamada Backwaters
description: The main houseboat hub on Vembanad Lake, and the venue of the Nehru Trophy snake-boat race.
tip: Compare licensed operators

name: Alappuzha Beach
description: A broad beach with a 150-year-old pier and lighthouse.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Marari Beach
description: A quiet fishing-village beach north of Alappuzha town.
tip: Easy access via village lanes; limited facilities.

name: Kuttanad Toddy Shops
description: Traditional toddy shops serve fiery Kuttanad food — duck roast, fish curry and tapioca. Food-only visits are common.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
description: A UNESCO-listed baroque church in Old Goa that holds the relics of St. Francis Xavier.
tip: Dress modestly

name: Palolem Beach
description: A palm-fringed crescent bay in South Goa with calm water and kayaking.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Fort Aguada
description: A 17th-century Portuguese fort and lighthouse overlooking the Mandovi estuary.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Dudhsagar Falls
description: A four-tiered waterfall on the Goa–Karnataka border, often reached by jeep through the Bhagwan Mahaveer sanctuary.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Divar Island
description: A sleepy river island of Portuguese houses and paddy fields, reached by free ferry.
tip: Ferry from Old Goa or Ribandar; cycling recommended.

name: Butterfly Beach
description: A small cove near Palolem reached by boat or a forest trail.
tip: Boat or trail only; no facilities.

name: Panaji Fish Thali Joints
description: Busy local restaurants in Panaji are known for fish thalis with Goan curry, rice and fried fish.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Goan Bakeries
description: Village bakeries (poders) sell poi bread and traditional sweets like bebinca.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Solang Valley
description: A side valley known for paragliding, zorbing and winter snow sports.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Hadimba Devi Temple
description: A 16th-century wooden pagoda-style temple set in a cedar forest.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Atal Tunnel & Sissu
description: The long highway tunnel under the Rohtang ridge leads to Sissu in Lahaul with waterfalls and snow peaks.
tip: Permits/road rules change — check locally

name: Jogini Falls
description: A waterfall above Vashisht village reached by a pleasant walk through orchards.
tip: About an hour's uphill walk; uneven trail.

name: Sethan Village
description: A small Buddhist hamlet above Prini, popular for snowshoeing and igloo stays in winter.
tip: Narrow mountain road; snow chains may be needed in winter.

name: Old Manali Cafés
description: Riverside cafés in Old Manali serve trout, wood-fired pizza and Himachali dishes.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Jantar Mantar
description: A UNESCO-listed collection of 18th-century astronomical instruments, including a giant sundial.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Panna Meena ka Kund
description: A symmetrical 16th-century stepwell near Amber, famous for its criss-cross stairs.
tip: Short walk from Amber; climbing on the steps may be restricted.

name: Pyaaz Kachori Shops
description: Jaipur's famous onion kachoris are best eaten hot from old sweet-and-snack shops near the station and old city.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Rajasthani Thali Restaurants
description: Traditional restaurants serve unlimited Rajasthani thalis with dal baati churma and gatte ki sabzi.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Lakeside Rooftop Restaurants
description: Rooftop restaurants around Gangaur Ghat serve Rajasthani dishes with lake views.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Pangong Tso
description: A long high-altitude lake that shifts between shades of blue, about 5 hours from Leh over Chang La.
tip: Inner Line Permit may be required

name: Thiksey Monastery
description: A 12-storey hilltop monastery resembling the Potala Palace, known for its morning prayers.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Nubra Valley
description: Sand dunes, double-humped camels and the Diskit monastery beyond Khardung La.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Hemis Shukpachan
description: A quiet village of juniper groves and homestays on the Sham valley trail.
tip: Village roads; homestays are basic. High altitude.

name: Leh Main Bazaar Kitchens
description: Small Ladakhi and Tibetan kitchens around the main bazaar serve warming noodle soups and butter tea.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Lakshman Jhula Area
description: The famous suspension-bridge area lined with temples, cafés and ashrams on both banks of the Ganga.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Triveni Ghat Aarti
description: The evening Ganga aarti with lamps, chants and floating offerings.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: White-Water Rafting (Shivpuri)
description: Graded rapids on the Ganga between Shivpuri and Rishikesh, run by licensed operators.
tip: Use licensed operators only

name: Neer Garh Waterfall
description: A series of small cascades and pools reached by a short uphill trail.
tip: Steep but short trail with steps.

name: Tapovan Cafés
description: Health-food cafés in Tapovan serve vegetarian bowls, chai and river views.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Tiger's Leap
description: A cliff-edge viewpoint over a deep valley, with seasonal waterfalls in the monsoon.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Karla Caves
description: Buddhist rock-cut caves with one of the largest ancient chaitya halls in India.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Lonavala Chikki Shops
description: Lonavala is famous for chikki, a jaggery-and-nut brittle sold all along the main road.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: White Rann at Dhordo
description: A seemingly endless white salt desert, magical on full-moon nights.
tip: A permit is required — usually issued at Bhirandiyara

name: Bhujodi Craft Village
description: A weaving village where artisans demonstrate handloom techniques.
tip: Village lanes; ask before photographing workshops.

name: Tiger Hill Sunrise
description: A famous sunrise point where the first light hits Kanchenjunga.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway
description: The UNESCO-listed narrow-gauge railway, with joy rides to Ghum and the Batasia Loop.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Chowrasta Tea Rooms
description: Tea rooms around the Mall serve first-flush Darjeeling tea and momos.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
description: A Shinto shrine famous for thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up Mount Inari.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Kinkaku-ji
description: The Golden Pavilion, a Zen temple covered in gold leaf reflected in a pond.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
description: Towering bamboo paths in western Kyoto, near the Tenryu-ji temple.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Otagi Nenbutsu-ji
description: A quiet temple in Arashiyama with over a thousand moss-covered, expressive stone rakan statues.
tip: Uphill walk or bus; some steps.

name: Nishiki Market
description: A narrow covered market street known as "Kyoto's kitchen", with pickles, tofu and sweets.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Tegallalang Rice Terraces
description: Sculpted rice terraces using the traditional subak irrigation system.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary
description: Forest temples home to hundreds of long-tailed macaques.
tip: Keep food and loose items out of sight

name: Tukad Cepung Waterfall
description: A waterfall inside a cave-like canyon where light beams pour through the rock.
tip: Steep stairs and wading through shallow water.

name: Ubud Warungs
description: Family-run warungs serve Balinese rice plates and roast specialities.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Government Botanical Garden
description: Terraced gardens laid out in the 19th century, with a fossilised tree trunk, glasshouses and the annual flower show in May.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Ooty Lake
description: An artificial lake built in 1824, popular for boating and lakeside rides.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Doddabetta Peak
description: The highest peak in the Nilgiris, with a telescope house and views across the hills on clear mornings.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Nilgiri Mountain Railway
description: The UNESCO-listed rack railway between Mettupalayam and Ooty, climbing through tunnels and tea country.
tip: Book well ahead; seats sell out

name: Avalanche Lake
description: A remote lake inside protected shola forest, visited by forest-department eco-tourism vehicles.
tip: Only via forest-department vehicles; limited daily slots.

name: Ooty Homemade Chocolate Shops
description: Ooty is known for its homemade chocolates sold at shops around Charing Cross and Commercial Road.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Kodaikanal Lake
description: The star-shaped lake at the heart of town, circled by a 5 km path for walking, cycling and horse rides.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Coaker's Walk
description: A paved cliff-edge path with valley views — on lucky days, you can see your shadow on the clouds (Brocken spectre).
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Pillar Rocks
description: Three granite pillars rising about 120 m from the valley, often wrapped in cloud.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Vattakanal Falls
description: A small village and waterfall below town, a starting point for gentle walks with views over the plains.
tip: Steep path from the road; some sections unpaved.

name: Kodai Bakeries
description: Small bakeries near the bazaar are popular for sandwiches, brownies and hot chocolate after a cold walk.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Ramanathaswamy Temple
description: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas, famous for its long pillared corridors and 22 sacred wells (theerthams).
tip: Dress modestly

name: Dhanushkodi
description: A ghost town destroyed by the 1964 cyclone, at the tip of Pamban Island where the Bay of Bengal meets the Indian Ocean.
tip: Sea at Arichal Munai can be rough — avoid swimming

name: Pamban Bridges
description: Road and rail bridges across the Palk Strait linking Pamban Island to the mainland.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Memorial
description: A memorial to the former President at Peikarumbu, with exhibits on his life and work.
tip: Accessible building; parking available.

name: Shore Temple
description: An 8th-century granite temple overlooking the Bay of Bengal, one of the oldest structural stone temples in South India.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Pancha Rathas
description: Five monolithic chariot-shaped temples, each carved from a single rock.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Arjuna's Penance
description: A huge open-air bas-relief carved on two boulders, depicting gods, people and animals.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Tiger Cave
description: A rock-cut shrine with a crown of carved tiger-like heads, a few kilometres north of town.
tip: Short sandy walk from the road.

name: Othavadai Street Seafood
description: Restaurants on the lanes near the beach grill the day's catch.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Abbey Falls
description: A waterfall tumbling through coffee and spice estates near Madikeri, viewed from a hanging bridge.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Raja's Seat
description: A garden viewpoint in Madikeri where Kodava kings are said to have watched the sunset.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Namdroling Monastery
description: The Golden Temple at Bylakuppe, one of the largest Tibetan Buddhist teaching centres in India.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Dubare Elephant Camp
description: A forest-department camp on the Kaveri where visitors can watch elephants being bathed and cared for.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Mandalpatti Viewpoint
description: Grassy ridges above the clouds, reached by a rough jeep track.
tip: Jeep ride on rough track followed by a short uphill walk.

name: Kodava Homestay Kitchens
description: Many homestays serve home-style Kodava meals — the best way to taste the region's cuisine.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Mysore Palace
description: The Indo-Saracenic seat of the Wodeyar kings, illuminated with thousands of bulbs on Sunday evenings and during Dasara.
tip: Shoes are left outside

name: Chamundi Hill
description: A hill temple with a giant monolithic Nandi on the 1,000-step path, and views of the city.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Brindavan Gardens
description: Terraced gardens below the Krishnaraja Sagar dam, known for evening musical fountains.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary
description: River islets on the Kaveri that host nesting painted storks, pelicans and crocodiles, seen by boat.
tip: Easy paved paths; boats require stepping down to the jetty.

name: Mylari Dosa Joints
description: Mysuru is famous for its soft, butter-laden Mylari-style dosas served at small, busy eateries.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Devaraja Market Sweet Shops
description: Traditional sweet shops around Devaraja Market sell Mysore Pak, said to have originated in the palace kitchens.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Virupaksha Temple
description: A living temple at the head of Hampi Bazaar, with a towering gopuram, in worship since before the Vijayanagara empire.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Vittala Temple & Stone Chariot
description: The most ornate complex in Hampi, with the iconic stone chariot and the "musical" pillars.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Matanga Hill
description: The highest point near the ruins, with a famous sunrise view over the boulders and temples.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Anegundi Village
description: An older village across the Tungabhadra with crafts, quiet temples and the Anjanadri hill.
tip: Reached by coracle/ferry (seasonal) or a long road detour.

name: Riverside Cafés
description: Laid-back cafés near the bazaar and across the river serve thalis and traveller favourites.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Mullayanagiri
description: Karnataka's highest peak, with a small temple on top and grassland ridges all around.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Baba Budangiri
description: A range where coffee is said to have first been planted in India, home to a revered shrine.
tip: Check local timings before you go.

name: Jhari Falls
description: Also called Buttermilk Falls, reached by jeep through coffee estates.
tip: Rough jeep track then a short walk.

name: Estate Coffee Tastings
description: Several estates and town cafés offer freshly roasted local coffee.
tip: Check local timings before you go.
